newsitem.title: JAPAN: NCB problem loans bigger than its estimate - sources.
newsitem.headline: NCB problem loans bigger than its estimate - sources.

text.p: An investigation conducted by the Ministry of Finance (MOF) showed that Nippon Credit Bank Ltd (NCB) has an estimated 700 billion yen in loans which may be unrecoverable -- surpassing the bank's original estimate of 500 billion yen, financial sources said on Tuesday.

An NCB spokesman declined to confirm the size of such loans but said that the MOF has acknowledged after its investigation that NCB's plan to dispose of its problem loans in the last business year ended March 31 was reasonable.

"We think we can dispose of our problem loans under our five-year profit programme, and we believe that the outcome of the MOF's investigation will not cause any problem (with the bank's restructuring plan)," he said.
NCB had revealed the MOF's findings to other financial institutions on Monday, hoping to convince them to assist in its restructuring by buying new NCB shares, the sources said.
The financial institutions -- banks and insurers --are expected to decide whether or not they will buy the new NCB shares after scrutinising the MOF's report, they said.
The sources said that banks would likely agree on buying NCB's new shares as originally expected, though it may take some time for the life insurers to agree on the purchases.

For instance, Japan's biggest life insurer Nippon Life Insurance Co has said that it wanted NCB to explain in a reasonable manner why it should exchange subordinated loans it has extended to the bank with new NCB shares.
A Nippon Life spokesman said on Tuesday that the company has not yet received the answer to its question from NCB.
On April 1, NCB announced a restructuring programme in which it said that it would take various steps to boost its profit by some 50 billion yen over the next five years.
It said that it would withdraw from overseas operations and increase its capital by about 300 billion yen.

NCB said that it would ask banks to buy 70 billion yen worth of the ordinary share issue and life and non-life insurers a total of 97 billion yen, the equivalent of about half of their outstanding perpetual subordinated loans to NCB.

It also said a special fund set up by the government to deal with bad loans at failed housing loan firms, or "jusen", would buy 80 billion yen worth of the preferred stock issue and life and non-life insurers 43.7 billion yen, equivalent to a fourth of life and non-life insurers' outstanding subordinated loans to NCB.
